newsitem.title: USA: U.S spot prods slip on NYMEX, NYH gasoline weakens.
newsitem.headline: U.S spot prods slip on NYMEX, NYH gasoline weakens.

text.p: U.S. spot product prices fell sharply by late Monday amid a keen NYMEX selloff and an import-related easing of gasoline differentials in New York Harbor, players said.

January NYMEX heating oil tumbled 2.53 cents a gallon and January gasoline lost 0.92 cent on news the U.N. Monday had concluded an oil-for-food deal allowing Iraq to begin selling $2 billion worth of oil over six months.
Differentials on heating oil were little changed on the news, with New York material offered at about 0.20 cent over the print and 35th cycle Gulf Coast at 4.50 cents below.

But New York heating oil traders said the tumbling NYMEX values sent sellers into hiding. "All my sellers seem to have evaporated," one player said, adding, "I guess they didn't want to sell that low."
Differentials on New York Harbor gasoline weakened across the board, players said, slipping a half cent on conventional unleaded with offers at a half cent over January futures, traders said.
"Several cargoes are expected in the next five days and are putting some pressure on prices," one New York trader said, adding there was little interest in reformulated "A5" grade.

Traders said arrivals of significant amounts of imported gasoline blendstocks helped undercut differentials on premium and reformulated grades, with NYH "A9"-grade oxygenated reformulated 87-octane material weakening a full 2.50 cents to 5.50 cents over the print.

In a widely anticipated move, U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali approved the limited Iraqi oil-for-food sales Monday, which ensured bearish momentum in the futures market througout the day.
-- Ransdell Pierson, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
